misconception_pool.misconception: Digital safety guidelines only apply when connecting to public networks outside the home.

misconception_pool.misconception: Deleting an embarrassing photo or message from a social media app permanently erases every copy from the internet.
misconception_pool.fact: Recipients can capture screenshots immediately, and remote servers often retain cached backups long after a user deletes a post.

misconception_pool.misconception: Private or incognito browser windows hide your identity and online messages from websites and internet providers.
misconception_pool.fact: Incognito mode only prevents the local device from saving browsing history; websites and networks still log your IP address and traffic.

misconception_pool.misconception: Online accounts displaying a teenager's profile photo and mutual friends are always operated by real peers.
misconception_pool.fact: Imposters frequently scrape public photos and add mutual contacts to build convincing fake profiles that deceive young users.

misconception_pool.misconception: Replying to a cyberbully or predator to demand that they stop is the safest way to resolve online harassment.
misconception_pool.fact: Engaging escalates harassment; Scouts should stop replying immediately, save screenshots as evidence, block the sender, and tell an adult.

Integrated Circuit Breakthrough: Silicon microchips allowed engineers to shrink room size mainframes into desktops.

misconception_pool.misconception: Early mainframes possessed computational architectures fundamentally identical to modern portable smartphones.
misconception_pool.fact: Modern microprocessors contain billions of nanoscale transistors operating at gigahertz switching frequencies.

misconception_pool.misconception: Early electronic computers like ENIAC stored data on magnetic hard drives and displayed output on video monitors.
misconception_pool.fact: First-generation computers used thousands of vacuum tubes for logic and relied on paper punch cards and plugboards for input and output.

misconception_pool.misconception: Moore's Law is a physical law of nature that guarantees computer processor clock speeds will double every two years.
misconception_pool.fact: Moore's Law is an empirical observation about transistor density on integrated circuits, and heat limits have slowed clock speed gains.

misconception_pool.misconception: The World Wide Web and the internet were invented at the same time as a single communication system.
misconception_pool.fact: Packet-switched networks like ARPANET began in the late 1960s, while Tim Berners-Lee created the World Wide Web protocols around 1990.

misconception_pool.misconception: Modern smartphones have less raw computing power than the mainframe computers used during the Apollo moon landings.
misconception_pool.fact: A single modern smartphone processor executes billions of instructions per second, millions of times faster than the Apollo Guidance Computer.

misconception_pool.misconception: Digital audio files store continuous sound waves directly onto storage media without sampling.
misconception_pool.fact: Digitization converts analog waveforms into discrete binary numbers using defined sampling rates and bit depths.

misconception_pool.misconception: Converting a low-quality MP3 or JPEG file into a lossless format like WAV or PNG restores the original lost detail.
misconception_pool.fact: Lossy compression permanently discards data during encoding, so converting to a lossless format never restores the discarded detail.

misconception_pool.misconception: Increasing the pixel dimensions of a digital image by stretching it on screen increases its true optical resolution.
misconception_pool.fact: Stretching an existing bitmap only enlarges or interpolates existing pixels without capturing any new optical detail from the scene.

misconception_pool.misconception: Digital audio recorders store continuous smooth sound waves directly inside flash memory chips.
misconception_pool.fact: Analog-to-digital converters sample the sound wave thousands of times per second and quantize each sample into binary numbers.

misconception_pool.misconception: Lossless compression algorithms like ZIP reduce file sizes by throwing away unimportant characters and numbers.
misconception_pool.fact: Lossless compression replaces repeated byte patterns with shorter tokens so the exact original file can be reconstructed bit for bit.

misconception_pool.misconception: All internet web traffic routes exclusively through orbiting commercial satellites across space.
misconception_pool.fact: Fiber optic cables transmit binary data as pulses of light through reflective glass cores.

misconception_pool.misconception: Wi-Fi and cellular data connections carry internet traffic all the way across the world without using physical cables.
misconception_pool.fact: Wireless signals only bridge the short hop to a local router or cell tower, after which undersea and underground fiber-optic cables carry data.

misconception_pool.misconception: The top result returned by an internet search engine is always the most accurate and trustworthy source on a topic.
misconception_pool.fact: Search rankings reflect keyword relevance, link popularity, or paid advertising rather than independent verification of factual accuracy.

misconception_pool.misconception: An HTTPS padlock icon in the browser address bar proves that the website owner is honest and safe from phishing.
misconception_pool.fact: HTTPS only encrypts data in transit; phishing sites routinely obtain valid TLS certificates for deceptive domain names.

misconception_pool.misconception: Internet data travels from sender to receiver as a single unbroken stream over a dedicated circuit like a phone call.
misconception_pool.fact: TCP/IP breaks data into small numbered packets that route independently across hops and reassemble in order at the destination device.

requirements.lead_text: Do THREE of the following. For each project you complete, copy the files to a backup device and share the finished projects with your counselor.
requirements.req_text: Do THREE of the following. For each project you complete, copy the files to a backup device and share the finished projects with your counselor. (a) Using a spreadsheet or database program, develop a food budget for a patrol weekend campout OR create a troop roster that includes the name, rank, patrol, and telephone number of each Scout. Show your counselor that you can sort the roster by each of the following categories: rank, patrol, and alphabetically by name. (b) Using a word processor, write a draft letter inviting the parents or guardians of your troop's Scouts to a troop event. Resource: Word Processing Tutorial (video) (c) Using a graphics program, design and draw a campsite plan for your troop OR create a flyer for an upcoming troop event, incorporating text and some type of visual such as a photograph or an illustration. (d) Using a presentation software program, develop a report about a topic approved by your counselor. For your presentation, create at least five slides, with each one incorporating text and some type of visual such as a photograph or an illustration. (e) Using a digital device, take a picture of a troop activity. Send or transfer this image to a device where it can be shared with your counselor. (f) Make a digital recording of your voice, transfer the file to a different device, and have your counselor play back the recording. (g) Create a blog and use it as an online journal of your Scouting activities, including group discussions and meetings, campouts, and other events. Include at least five entries and two photographs or illustrations. Share your blog with your counselor. You need not post the blog to the internet; however, if you choose to go live with your blog, you must first share it with your parent or guardian AND counselor AND get their approval. (h) Create a webpage for your troop, patrol, school, or place of worship. Include at least three articles and two photographs or illustrations. Include at least one link to a website of interest to your audience. You need not post the page to the internet; however, if you decide to do so, you must first share the webpage with your parent or guardian AND counselor AND get their approval.

misconception_pool.misconception: Discarded electronic circuit boards dissolve harmlessly when buried in standard municipal landfill waste.
misconception_pool.fact: Lead solder and mercury switches in discarded circuit boards leach into ground water if landfilled.

misconception_pool.misconception: Tossing old cell phones and circuit boards into a municipal curbside recycling bin ensures they are recycled safely.
misconception_pool.fact: Curbside bins are built for paper, glass, and cans; lithium batteries in e-waste frequently spark fires inside sorting trucks and plants.

misconception_pool.misconception: Dragging personal files to the desktop trash can or recycle bin removes your private data before donating a computer.
misconception_pool.fact: Standard deletion only removes file pointers, so recovery tools can read private data until the drive is securely overwritten or wiped.

misconception_pool.misconception: All companies advertising free electronics drop-off dismantle toxic components safely inside regulated domestic facilities.
misconception_pool.fact: Uncertified collectors often ship e-waste overseas for open-air burning; look for R2 or e-Stewards certification to verify safe processing.

misconception_pool.misconception: Modern flat-screen devices and circuit boards contain only harmless plastics and aluminum with no toxic heavy metals.
misconception_pool.fact: Electronic devices still contain hazardous substances like lead solder, cadmium, mercury, and brominated flame retardants.

requirements.req_text: Do ONE of the following: (a) Explore careers related to the Digital Technology merit badge. Research one career to learn about the training and education needed, costs, job prospects, salary, job duties, and career advancement. Your research methods may include, with your parent or guardian's permission, an internet or library search, an interview with a professional in the field, or a visit to a location where people in this career work. Discuss with your counselor both your findings and what about this profession might make it an interesting career. (b) Explore how you could use knowledge and skills from the Digital Technology merit badge to pursue a hobby or interest. Research any training needed, expenses, and organizations that promote or support it. Discuss with your counselor what short-term and long-term goals you might have if you pursued this.

misconception_pool.misconception: Entering a software engineering career requires no formal technical training or project portfolio.
misconception_pool.fact: Information security analysts need certifications and strong foundations in networking, cryptography, and operating systems.

misconception_pool.misconception: Every high-paying digital technology career requires a four-year university degree in computer science before you can get hired.
misconception_pool.fact: Many network, cloud, and cybersecurity roles hire candidates with associate degrees, apprenticeships, or vendor certifications.

misconception_pool.misconception: National average salary figures represent the exact starting paycheck a newly hired entry-level technician will earn in any city.
misconception_pool.fact: Entry-level pay is typically in the lower quartile of national medians and varies widely by local cost of living and credentials.

misconception_pool.misconception: Digital technology in an industrial facility is limited to the desktop computers and laptops inside the main administrative office.
misconception_pool.fact: Industrial facilities also rely on programmable logic controllers, barcode scanners, automated sensors, and inventory systems.

misconception_pool.misconception: Initial technical training is enough to sustain a digital career for decades without ongoing study or credential renewal.
misconception_pool.fact: Digital professionals must complete continuing education and renew technical certifications every few years to keep up with new systems.

options: A. Use your home street address and birth year as your password across all websites so you never forget it.
B. Use long, unique pass phrases with multi-factor authentication, never share PII.
C. Disable firewall and operating system security updates because patches slow down video streaming and gaming.

choices: A. Use your home street address and birth year as your password across all websites so you never forget it.

patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: B. Use long, unique pass phrases with multi-factor authentication, never share PII (such as home address, phone number, school schedule, or financial details) publicly, verify links before clicking, and include a parent or trusted adult in digital communications.
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (B): Digital Technology Requirement 1 emphasizes safeguarding PII, using strong unique pass phrases with multi-factor authentication, keeping software updated, avoiding phishing links, and following BSA Youth Protection digital rules.

options: A. Lossless compression permanently removes unimportant numbers to save space
B. Lossless compression restores the exact original data without losing a single character or instruction
C. Lossy compression only works on computers built before 1990
D. Lossless compression automatically converts text files into MP3 audio
choices: A. Lossless compression permanently removes unimportant numbers to save space
B. Lossless compression restores the exact original data without losing a single character or instruction
C. Lossy compression only works on computers built before 1990
D. Lossless compression automatically converts text files into MP3 audio
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: B. Lossless compression restores the exact original data without losing a single character or instruction
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (B): Lossless compression reduces file size while preserving 100 percent of the original data, which is essential for text, spreadsheets, and executable programs where missing bytes would corrupt the file (p. 26).
